newsitem.title: USA: Miami lobbyist pleads guilty in city hall scandal.
newsitem.headline: Miami lobbyist pleads guilty in city hall scandal.

text.p: A lobbyist pleaded guilty Friday to obstructing justice in a bribery investigation that resulted in criminal charges against three City of Miami officials.
Lobbyist Jorge DeCardenas, 52, had been scheduled to go to trial Monday on eight counts of conspiracy, bribery, money laundering, wire fraud, mail fraud and witness tampering.
He pleaded guilty to one count of obstructing justice and the other seven counts were dismissed. DeCardenas faces up to 10 years in prison although sentencing guidlines call for 10 to 16 months.

Former City Manager Cesar Odio and former City Commissioner Miller Dawkins previously pleaded guilty in the case. Former Miami Finance Director Manohar Surana, who secretly taped conversations that implicated the others, has also agreed to plead guilty to unspecified charges.
DeCardenas acknowledged in the plea agreement that he collected and distributed kickbacks from an insurance company that held a city contract.
Dawkins is serving a 27-month prison term on a bribery charge. Odio faces 10 to 16 months in prison when he is sentenced Aug. 26 on a charge of obstructing justice.

The charges stem from the federal government's ongoing "Operation Greenpalm" investigation of public finance corruption in Miami and Dade County. The probe also fouses on whether government officials accepted bribes in connection with municipal bond deals.
